title: Notes of Ministry - 39 - February 1976

source.file: Various/Notes of Ministry - 39 - February 1 (2425)/Notes of Ministry - 39 - Februa - Various.epub

paragraphs.text: As our brother was praying these scriptures came distinctly to one’s mind and the thought of comfort. This is a wonderful occasion. It is recorded in Psalm 116: 15, “Precious in the sight of Jehovah is the death of his saints”. It is a precious occasion, beloved, for all heaven is interested in what we are about to do in the burial of our sister, one well known to most, if not all, of us here. She died in the Lord, she was fully in the testimony, but the Lord came and took her. I have been impressed with the way Peter speaks of “the hidden man of the heart, in the incorruptible ornament of a meek and quiet spirit”, 1 Peter 3: 4. This is something those of us cherish who visited our sister from time to time, “a meek and quiet spirit, which in the sight of God is of great price”.

What a wonderful encouragement it is to us all, what a comfort, to be in an area in which all heaven is interested. Things are transpiring around us in the scene through which we are passing, but this occasion is outstanding, all heaven being interested in the burial of a saint. I believe that scripture in Psalm 116, “Precious in the sight of Jehovah is the death of his saints”, shows that every saint who dies in the Lord and falls asleep through Jesus reminds God of the death of His beloved Son. There is an affinity between the death of a believer and the death of His Son, our Lord Jesus, the One who died for us, the One who lives for us, the One who is going to come soon to take us all to be with Himself. What a glorious, triumphant outlook we have, dear brethren!—and what encouragement it gives us to be in the light and joy of these precious thoughts.

It is wonderful to see how the Spirit of God is operating; we have seen it in our sister, a meek and quiet spirit, an adornment, and we can speak of her as an assembly person. The assembly is composed of persons like ourselves, who believe on the Lord Jesus and have the Spirit. The Lord Jesus loved the assembly and delivered Himself up for it, and He is going to present it to Himself glorious, without spot or wrinkle, and that day is coming soon. But now we are about to commit the body of our beloved sister to the Lord in anticipation of His coming to transform it into conformity to His body of glory (Philippians 3: 21). What joy marks the outlook of the believer, the joy of the first resurrection, “Blessed and holy he who has part in the first resurrection” (Revelation 20: 6), and that is the outlook of every true believer. As we are about to commit the body of our beloved sister, the last service of love, let us take courage as we think of what she suffered and what she took on through it, a meek and quiet spirit, subjection to the Lord, obedience to His word.

I believe she was a subject of Paul’s ministry and she continued to the end having that glorious moment always in her heart, the coming of the Lord. The last words she uttered in our presence were, ‘The Lord is coming and His reward is with Him’ (Revelation 22: 12). Think of one just going to be with the Lord and thinking of His reward, and that is the normal hope of every believer. It is a comfort to every one of us, the prospect of being with that glorious Man where He is and as He is, in that scene where He is supreme. O, beloved brethren, let the value of this moment affect us all for I believe it is intended to bring about sobriety and lowliness of mind in view of our being more and more intimate with the Persons of the Godhead.

In the scripture I read in John 14 the Lord Jesus was speaking to His disciples, just as He would speak to us now by the Spirit, “Let not your heart be troubled; ye believe on God, believe also on me. In my Father’s house there are many abodes; were it not so, I had told you—for I go to prepare you a place; and if I go and shall prepare you a place, I am coming again and shall receive you to myself, that where I am ye also may be”. Many say they believe on God, but when you speak to them of the Lord Jesus it is a different matter. Jesus is the One who was despised and left alone of men, but the true believer who owns His authority as Lord and recognises His headship comes in for the fulness of the blessing, and God has nothing but blessing in mind for all. He has provided everything for us in that glorious Man, the Man Christ Jesus. The scripture in chapter 16 relates to something our sister possessed—joy. The Lord says, “Your joy no one takes from you”. That is something we all need to cherish, His joy in our souls as having a link with Christ where He is and as He is. May the Lord add His blessing to what has been said, for His name’s sake.

I believe that the Lord Jesus has a voice for us in each death that takes place. As exercised in relation to the death of our sister what has impressed itself on me is the word of the Lord Jesus in John 15: 8, “In this is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit”, and I feel He would use this occasion to stimulate the desire in each of our hearts that, for the rest of our time, our lives might be more fruitful for God. Our sister has “come to the grave in a ripe age”, not only in old age, but in a “ripe age”, and that suggests maturity, spiritual maturity. Those of us who have had the privilege of being near our sister in recent years have witnessed the maturing of the work of God so that she was ready, waiting, and willing just to go to be with Christ. Christ was her all. We also saw a manifestation of the spirit of Christ, as our brother has said, and that in two outstanding features. One was patience, reminding us of the patience of Jesus, the patience of the Christ as He awaits His heavenly bride. The other was her capacity for suffering; what she suffered no one knew but herself and the Lord Jesus. This reminded us of the unique capacity of Jesus for suffering, for He took on sufferings that no creature could take on, sufferings for sin, the atoning sufferings—
‘None could follow there, blest Saviour,
When Thou didst for sins atone’.

But her ‘season’ has come, as it says here, “As a shock of corn is brought in in its season”—a very homely touch; not a stalk of corn, not a sheaf of corn, but a shock of corn, which means a number of sheaves and suggests a life that has been fruitful for God. We can say that of our sister, that her life has yielded much for God; but nothing is lost, it is brought in, the Lord has brought it in, garnered it, and it is safely housed. It but awaits the body of glory.

Well, dear brethren, she is gone and we are left and I desire that our lives henceforth might be more and more fruitful for God. The Lord Jesus says in John 15: 5, “He that abides in me, and I in him, he bears much fruit”. May the sorrow of this occasion lead our hearts more to Christ; may we be to Him (Romans 7: 4); may we abide in Him, and be held constantly in our affections in relation to Christ, so that He may have the supreme place in our hearts and minds in view of our bearing more fruit for God. This is the divine intent, for the day is coming soon when the wheat will be brought together into His granary. The “shock” has gone before, the fulness of the harvest will soon be here, the wheat harvest, the Lord Jesus coming to take His assembly. Every vestige of His work from Pentecost to the rapture, the wheat, will be brought together into His granary. It is “his wheat”, as it says in Matthew 3: 12; it is what corresponds to Himself. He was the lonely grain of wheat, as we sing, ‘O how precious was that lonely Corn of Wheat’ which fell into the ground and died, but His death has been so productive, so fruitful for God! What a harvest!

We can think of the living saints, but there are far more in their graves, myriads of saints in their graves. What a sowing there has been in “that field”, as it says in verse 44 of this chapter. He “buys that field”—the earth is His on the basis of purchase. Men think of it as theirs, but it belongs to Christ, and He is using it at the present time as a burying place for His saints; the dead saints are being sown in faith. The trees are there too—it says that in Genesis 23 where Abraham buys the field and the cave that was in it and the trees in all its borders; that could suggest the living saints. The dead saints would be in the cave of Machpelah awaiting resurrection. Christ’s resurrection being the assurance that they will be raised. Oh that moment is soon to come! The saints are maturing for glory.

This chapter in Matthew shows that the world is maturing for judgment; the tares are something sown which is like the real thing, but the sons of the evil one are maturing for judgment. The saints are maturing for glory and very soon the Lord will give the assembling shout and bring the wheat together, every blood-bought saint brought together and taken into His granary to be safely housed for eternity. In the meantime, beloved brethren, I desire that more of the ‘wheat’ may be seen with us, more correspondence to Christ. In this scene, where evil is developing fast, may we be marked off as persons who are more like Jesus and thus yielding more and more for the pleasure of the heart of God. May it be so for His name’s sake.

articles.title: STABILITY IN THE PRESENCE OF DEATH
articles.author: J. Mair
articles.meeting: Words at the burial of Mrs

paragraphs.text: I am impressed, dear brethren, with the stability that enters into our souls on an occasion such as this. Instability marks the whole scene through which we pass, but here we have a scene of stability. The field that our brother referred to was assured to Abraham for a possession. The Lord Jesus has been pleased to put our sister to sleep and no one can challenge His right. Who would dare to? It is His own personal service, “asleep through Jesus”, and then at His coming He will yet serve her as He will serve each one of His own. He will not delegate the service to an angel, but “The Lord himself, with an assembling shout, with archangel’s voice and with trump of God, shall descend from heaven; and the dead in Christ shall rise first; then we, the living who remain, shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air”. It is the personal service of Christ.

I recall visiting our sister a few weeks ago and the last audible words we heard in her weakness were, ‘Jesus is becoming more precious’. Can you and I say that in the presence of death? Do we know Him as the resurrection and the life? Can we say in the presence of the article of death, in the assurance of our souls, that Jesus is becoming ever more precious to us? Think of the stability of the position. It says of Abraham, “the father of all them that believe …” (Romans 4: 11), that he believed God and He reckoned it to him as righteousness (Genesis 15: 6). You and I come in in the same way. The assurance of an eternity of glory with our Lord Jesus is in coming the same way as Abraham, who believed God and it was reckoned to him as righteousness, Romans 4: 3. It is the righteousness of faith, another kind of righteousness, not by works nor by the law, but righteousness of faith.

The position is stable. What does Mamre speak of? Stability. Earlier in this book Abraham was sitting by the oaks of Mamre (Genesis 18: 1). Think of what came to him there in the stability of his own soul, and that belongs to us, in stability, as we recognise our precious links with Christ in what He has achieved through going into death and rising again. Mamre antedates the whole world system and it is assured to us on the principle of faith. O, dear brethren, what stability this gives! Our brother referred to the verse, “Precious in the sight of Jehovah is the death of his saints”. What assurance it gives us when we know that the power of death, which no human power could challenge, has been challenged and met by that glorious Man who is at the right hand of God and who is about to come for His saints. O that each one here, in the inward secret of their souls, may be conscious of this link with Christ, the One who is going to exercise His power in love to raise our sister from the grave.
It says that the cave that was in the field was “assured to Abraham for a possession of a sepulchre by the sons of Heth”. Our hymn (No. 375) said—
‘Thy precious blood the purchase price
To be with Thee in paradise’.

The field was purchased for four hundred shekels of silver. Who can challenge the Lord’s rights in a situation like this? It is a position unshakable and unchallengeable. We can rest our souls, dear brethren, on what our blessed Lord Jesus has done. Our brother referred to the cave that is in the field, and we are about to lay our sister in the grave; we commit her body to the Lord until that glorious resurrection day. It says “the cave that was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all its borders round about, were assured to Abraham for a possession”. Think of that, the trees that were in its borders, that which is distinctly defined, the living saints there in testimony, to put it in current language. Today there is a distinct border marked out by the trees, “The trees of the Lord are full of sap”. Psalm 104: 16 (A.V.), like our sister going out in a ripe age. The trees of the Lord are full of sap and clearly define the borders of Abraham’s possession. O, dear brethren, what comfort, what assurance this begets in our souls! May the Lord bless the word.

The simple link in these scriptures, dear brethren, is the outshining. It says of Jesus, “His garments became shining, exceeding white as snow, such as fuller on earth could not whiten them”. Everything in Him, as we know, is perfect. There is no question of limitation with Him, although as Man He accepted the limitations that manhood would impose upon Him, but I am thinking of the perfection of the shining out in Him of the wonderful knowledge of God. It was a unique privilege for these three men. Jesus said, “There are some of those standing here that shall not taste death until they shall have seen the kingdom of God come in power”. We have already been reminded in these meetings that the kingdom of God is not in word but in power.

That is to say it is effective. There may be with us an understanding of the word ‘kingdom’, but I think what the Lord would draw our attention to is the power of that. As the Spirit is present, giving efficacy to the ministry as it reaches us, it comes in power so that the kingdom of God is not just a theory but its moral sway in the souls of the saints is known.

So Jesus says, here, “The kingdom of God come in power”. Then He takes these three men “up on a high mountain by themselves apart”. I suppose it would have some bearing on the service He was going to give them. We say it is sovereign, but I doubt not that the Lord’s sovereignty, as all else, is based on His wisdom. His selection was based on wisdom. Sovereignty is not arbitrary. He has a right to do what He will in His own affairs. He chooses Paul, or Peter, or it may be Mark. ‘I do’, He says, “what I will in my own affairs”, Matthew 20: 15. It is a good thing, beloved brethren, for us just simply to acknowledge that and allow the Lord to do what He will among us. So that persons who laboured throughout the day, you recall (if we might turn aside for a moment), received a denarius, just exactly the same as those who laboured only at the end of the day (see Matthew 20). ‘Most unfair’, men say, ‘that I should have been working in this industry for forty years and am earning no more than someone who has only been in it three months’. That is what men say. We must recognise, dear brethren, that even among men, a man has a right to do what he will in his own affairs. What he would do normally would be wise. So each of them receives a denarius. On the face of it, it seems unfair, but I think we need to bow to the Lord’s own sovereign actions. As we have sometimes been reminded, Mr. Raven said there is nothing that the human heart hates more than the sovereignty of God (see F.E.R. N.S. Vol. 7, p.253), i.e. His right to do as He pleases.

So Jesus takes these three men (there is no evidence in this passage that the others resented it), but He takes them because He has in mind that there should be something effective, that they should witness what presently should have part in their own service in the testimony. So it says, “He was transfigured before them”. I should like to have witnessed that, would not you? But it is not my lot to have witnessed it. What a day it was in which they lived! What a privilege, dear brethren, it was; a suffering privilege, maybe, but what a privilege to get such a vision of “the kingdom of God come in power”. It was evidence to them that everything eventually would be put into effect when God operated to bring to pass the great administration of the fulness of times that everything should be headed up in, and be under, Christ. How great Christ is! You can understand God calling attention to Him. Evidently Peter tried to enter into the conversation. How gracious is the intervention, calling attention to the perfection and glory of Jesus and what He was to the Father. “This is my beloved Son— hear him”. We need to hear Him, dear brethren. Do you think He is speaking today? When I say ‘today’ I mean not this particular day in 1974, although He is speaking in that, but in our day. Are you prepared to hear Him?

These three men were evidently young; we have sometimes been reminded that John was possibly not much more than seventeen. Our brother referred last evening to two young men, David—he was seventeen, I think—and Joseph. They both had to suffer in the testimony at a tender age. They began young and both finished. I suppose David was something around seventy when he died, and Joseph was a hundred and ten. They went on and they went through. These young men on the mount had their privileged part in the testimony as affected by what they saw shining in Jesus. It shone, of course, in lowliness. ‘All that shone in Christ once humbled’, the hymn says, ‘There expands in glory’s light’. There was the shining of grace here in that lowly, heavenly Man. If we say that of the assembly we can surely say it of Him. Lowliness; an unearthly witness of heavenly things on earth, all the glory of Jesus here in lowliness.

Now as on the mountain it says, “His garments became shining”, all the purity of His heavenly associations, “exceeding white as snow such as fuller on earth could not whiten them”. Who could whiten the garments of Jesus? We have sometimes been reminded of the words of Mr. Darby that Jesus was absolutely and infinitely good enough to be always perfect, and being absolutely and infinitely perfect, He was always absolutely and infinitely good. But the shining is what has impressed me in the passage. We get a reference to the fuller in Scripture and the fuller’s lye, and the need for the purifying of the sons of Levi, but was there any need in the perfect Servant Prophet for the application of anything from the fuller? No; all there was infinitely perfect, and the shining such as is almost indescribable, the whiteness and the purity, all that was innate in that blessed Man shining out.

Then it says, “There appeared to them Elias with Moses”. It does not say ‘in glory’ here but just that they appeared, “talking with Jesus”. I suppose they were suited to that scene. How would they know that it was “Elias with Moses”? How would Peter know it, or John, or James, or Mark the writer? The Spirit of God does not enlighten us about that but He does tell us that they were there, I doubt not that they were there as suitable, but they must have been there as having a right to be there as based on the precious death of Jesus. How wonderful that is! He was on the way to the cross. If Moses and Elias were to have a part on the mount, they must have it through the work of Jesus, in the same way as Paul or Peter, James or John, or any other person. Everyone who has a part there has it on the basis of the precious death of Jesus. This is the Person who was going to die. What moral glory shone out in Jesus here, what moral and, I suppose we could say, spiritual glory shone out in Him. These are the holy associations to which He was proper, heavenly associations that man never contaminated, having no moral contact with the world whatever; they shone there in absolute perfection.

No doubt that shining was to affect the apostles so that later they too might shine. James, of course, was put to death by Herod. We might ask, what is the point? I doubt not that the impression of the shining of Jesus and the kingdom of God come in power strengthened him for what he had to suffer as a martyr. If Peter is to go through, the exceeding whiteness of the garments of Jesus would impress him. You could not think of him being associated with the world, or forming links with the world, or having part in their celebrations. Could you think that of James or Peter or John? They would think of the clearness and the purity, of the holy, heavenly associations of Jesus which they saw shining. So they were committed to it, and I believe it was effective. “The kingdom of God come in power” means that it affected them and I think, dear brethren, it is to affect us.

I read the second passage because here we have the shining through persons. It is not Jesus personally, but Paul and those that are with him and he says, “It is the God who spoke that out of darkness light should shine who has shone in our hearts for the shining forth of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ”. That was in those men. They were products of the work of the Spirit and in their word, walk and ways there was a “shining forth of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ”. Think of that, dear brethren, that there was then in persons, and I believe there is today, the expression in manner of life, in word, and walk, and ways, of what is shining in the face of that blessed Man in heaven. Note—“out of darkness light should shine”; that meant that Jesus must go into the darkness. He must settle every moral question, which He has done, and now in Him at the right hand of God the glory of God is shining. How is it seen here in testimony? It is seen in vessels. It may be that the vessels are broken. I suppose many of our dear brethren as they get older are conscious of the fact that the vessel is being broken. It may not be felt by young men, because most of them are strong. “The glory of young men is their strength”, Proverbs 20: 29. I doubt not that Paul, in all that he passed through, felt the breaking of the vessel, so that the light shone. It has been so often linked with Gideon’s men, the breaking of the pitchers and the shining of the light (see Judges 7).

What is the shining? It is really the shining of Christ as He shines above, and as these men moved around there would be before men the constant shining of what was in “the face of Jesus Christ”. Who is it there for? It is there for men. There at the right hand of God is the perfect expression of God’s thoughts for men. As the apostles moved around, I believe, they would have in mind that men should come into the gain of it, so there was a practical testimony, not just a preaching. A preaching is one thing, and we thank God for everyone who can preach, but thank God for every one in whose heart God has shone for the shining forth among men “of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ”. So we say, ‘Well, does that exist today? If so, where is it?’ Well, you know what Mr. Darby’s father said to him, ‘Make it better by one man, my son’. You come into it. Whether you are young or old, seventeen or seventy, you be exercised to come into it.

So even in a day of declension something of His glory is seen. You would not care to argue, would you, that the glory of God is no longer shining in the face of Jesus Christ? Who would dare to argue such a thing? But where is the expression of it? I believe and am persuaded that there has been the expression of it in the recovery. Many of us have witnessed it in men who have set forth “the knowledge of the glory of God” in themselves, suffering often. How much beloved Mr. Taylor suffered from opposition. When we think of the troubles through which we may have passed, what has often pressed in upon our spirits, think of him through a long life, with Satan’s opposition to destroy and overthrow the ministry. I think there was there, and in others too, some demonstration, some shining in the darkness here in this poor world, of what is shining in the face of Jesus Christ for all men. Well now, what about you? You may say to me, ‘What about you—sometimes you are not much of an advertisement for it’. I have humbly to admit that one day a little while ago one of the men at the office said to me, ‘Cheer up, Eddie, it may never happen’.

You see, I have to face it. Was that shining? Well, it was not shining. Maybe it was a problem causing a frown. We all have problems; but I think characteristically the saints here in the recovery are shining forth what is “in the face of Jesus Christ” for every man.

As we know, what is in Christ is for all men. It is laid hold of by faith, not by all, nevertheless it is there for all. So in Paul and his company—we love to think of them and learn from them—there was the practical expression, a reflection here in shining, of what was shining in Jesus on the mountain, “the kingdom of God come in power”. It was effective in them. We need to be exercised about this, dear brethren; not just to grasp the truth, but that it should be effective in the power and grace of the Spirit so that we should come into the shining, which is the shining of our Lord Jesus Christ seen in some in testimony, and carried forward in testimony. I think also, as I have said, that the Lord has graciously recovered it.

Is it going to continue? Shall we let it lapse? I will say this, it will never lapse, the Lord will see to that. Whether I am in it or not is another question. I desire to be in it in some little degree, but I will tell you something; I am inclined to shrink from it. I say to the Lord, ‘I would like to have an experience like Paul’s when Thou didst stand by him’. He might say to me, Are you prepared to be in the circumstances in which he was when he had it? You would like an angel of the Lord, or of the God, as Paul says, “whose I am and whom I serve” (Acts 27: 23) to stand by you? Well, are you prepared to be in a shipwreck?

There are certain circumstances in which that man was, which called out the sympathy of the Lord and gave him those unique experiences. So it tends to make you shrink. Do not shrink; go forward. That is what one has had to learn. Go forward, counting on His grace to sustain you in whatever circumstances you may find yourself, so that through it all there might be a little shining here in testimony; not just in word, but in walk and ways, a testimony to what God is as having been fully expressed in our Lord Jesus Christ.

Now we find a city in Revelation 21. “And there came one of the seven angels which had had the seven bowls full of the seven last plagues”. I suppose this is the great contrast to the false city, Babylon; there is no shining there. So when John saw this city coming down it did not look like a prison. Some cities might look like that. Of the false one it says, “a hold of every unclean and hated bird”, Revelation 18: 2. How solemn that is! Now it says it is one of the angels that had had the seven bowls; the angel would have some insight into all that they meant, would he not? He says, “Come here, I will shew thee ...”. I would like to be available like that, would not you? But I will say that this was not just sovereign. I do not doubt that the Lord took up John with this in view, but it was not just sovereign; he was a man who was able to be carried. “Come here, I will shew thee”. Have we eyes to see, dear brethren? Are we looking in the right direction? “I saw and behold, a door opened in heaven”, Revelation 4: 1. He obviously was not looking towards the earth, for then he would not have seen the door in heaven.

In which direction are you young men and women looking—towards the earth, bigger houses, bigger cars, bigger businesses, and the like? You would never see a door in heaven if that is your outlook. Do your business righteously, but do not let it hold you, do not let it grip you, do not let it absorb you, or you will miss the door open in heaven and the Spirit will not find you available for the angel to say, “Come here, I will shew thee”. O, I would like to see things like this, would not you? It says, “He carried me away in the Spirit”. I think if we set ourselves for spiritual experiences we shall be surprised what the Lord will do for us, even in these days. Now I commend it to all of us, not only to the young, but also to the older ones, what the Spirit of God will show us. It says he “showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of the heaven from God, having the glory of God”. I have often thought that she would have learned that from Jesus—“coming down”, in all the grace of heaven, but “having the glory of God”. It speaks of “her shining”, a heavenly body, so to speak, a luminary. As we have already said, not like a prison, but shining in beneficence, and all the provision needed for men coming down out of heaven. She belonged there. We have often been told that the origin of the assembly is heaven and her destiny is heaven. Here she is coming out “having the glory of God”.

O, dear brethren, we are looking forward to this! There is no shining in any in this world, save in those who know God. How dark! Men’s hearts are failing them for fear of those things that are coming upon the earth. Where will it end? There is no hope. All these things are in the minds and hearts of men, bringing almost despair. Of course, they turn it away with humour, but it rests in their hearts that they have no knowledge of what is going to happen. But we have; there is going to be a beneficent administration from a vessel “having the glory of God”, equal to that. It is not glory from God, but “the glory of God”. She is the product of divine workmanship—how great! As another has said, a creature in perfection, and all that shining out.

How will all that work out? “Thou be over five cities”; “be thou in authority over ten cities”, that is how it will work out in simple blessing for men, and all that God is will come into expression in the way of shining in that simple way. What about you and me? I love to think of that day. Mr. Raven did not claim to be much, did he? He said he hoped he would be counted worthy to carry a message. I am sure if he did he would shine, he would make the message shine. So if we can be but messenger boys, so to speak, in the world to come, we can make the position shine. I think every service rendered by every person belonging to the city—for, after all, it is composed of persons—will shine, so that God will be glorified in it as well as men being brought into blessing. May the Lord help us, dear brethren, that we may be exercised to come into the gain of the truth, that there may be in this day of darkness more simple shining among men so that they may see and understand what the disposition of God is towards them, and that through the gracious working of His Spirit others may be turned in faith to lay hold of what is in that Man at the right hand of God, “the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ”. How wonderful that is, but if it is to be known here it is known in vessels.

So, in brief, we have firstly the shining of Jesus, “His garments became shining, exceeding , white as snow, such as fuller on earth could not whiten them”, no touch could be added to what was there; then others coming into the testimony as understanding what is in that Man, and then finally the great consummation. There are no apologies, no changes; the city as it comes down is precisely what God originally intended. Dear brethren, the divine objective will be reached, the city will come down out of heaven just as God planned, as one has often said, without any modifications. It is not like men—‘Well, of course, that should have been a piece of oak there, but we were a bit short so we had to polish some deal and put it in’—that is man’s idea. Modified building is not the divine way. What God produces in the city, in creature perfection, is exactly what He originally intended in His purpose. May we take courage from it, dear brethren, and go forward in our own simple measure in our day, seeking to be here for His glory. May it be so for His name’s sake.

articles.title: THE NEED FOR ACTIVE FAITH
articles.author: A. Roy Steven
articles.place: Word in meeting for ministry, Brooklyn, N.Y.

paragraphs.text: Hebrews 11: 6; 10: 35–I just have a simple impression, dear brethren, regarding faith. Scripture reminds us that the present time is “God’s dispensation, which is in faith”, 1 Timothy 1: 4. Then in the scripture which is our charter it says that we should pursue righteousness, and the next thing is faith (2 Timothy 2: 22). I have long had the feeling that it was placed in that order by the writer in a methodical way, because if we are to do what is right as christians, what is right and pleasing in the sight of God, it requires faith. I have the impression that the Spirit of God would freshly energise us as to faith, because we are in a time when things are becoming very testing. Many of us are experiencing testing times in our households. Some younger people have gotten off the line of faith and are being controlled by what relates to sight. But faith would count on God, knowing that with God all things are possible. Faith is not controlled in any wise by circumstances, and the power of God comes in to help us as we are on the line of faith because the Holy Spirit is only free to operate as we are in active faith.

One has not much to say, but I feel that if we are to come substantially into the great things that God has prepared for us it requires active faith. From the divine side things remain intact; there is no change with God. I am thankful that we are being encouraged constantly as to the unchanging character of the love of God, and He would stimulate us and help us to see that He remains faithful despite all the unfaithfulness that has come in, and that what He has prepared for us (as we are told in Corinthians, “Things which eye has not seen, and ear not heard, and which have not come into man’s heart, which God has prepared for them that love him” (1 Corinthians 2: 9)) also remains intact. As we are in faith, dear brethren, the Spirit would help us to enter substantially into these things that God has prepared for them that love Him. Our scripture says, “Without faith it is impossible to please him”. Love is great, but we notice that in the list in 2 Timothy 2: 22 it says, righteousness, faith, then love. All God’s operations are in love, yet His love is flowing on a righteous basis; God is not showing His love unrighteously. So we need faith to accept all these things. Much of what we are experiencing, publicly, may be difficult to understand.

I do not think any of us would be presumptuous enough to think that we can fully understand the extensive movements of God at the present time, but then faith would say that all is well; God is not against us in any wise, God is for us, and in faith we can count on Him that He will see us through. When I refer to circumstances I do not mean in relation to assembly matters, because I believe that the order of things that we enjoy at the present time will go through to the end. Let us not in any wise think that there is going to be a great public revival; I do not think God is on that line; but what He is doing is reviving the affections of the saints; the Spirit of God is helping the saints to enter upon things in a more substantial, living and vital way. So we need faith to link on with that and to experience the help of the blessed Spirit.

The scripture in Hebrews 10 would encourage us. It says, “Cast not away therefore your confidence, which has great recompense. For ye have need of endurance in order that, having done the will of God, ye may receive the promise”. What a great promise we have, dear brethren, the promise of God linked on with the time when the Lord Jesus will come into His rights publicly. He who is now cast out by men, despised and rejected, will come into His rights in a public way and we shall have our part with Him. But, by the Spirit, how blessed it is that we are now able to have part with Christ in His present position. I trust that we will be encouraged, stimulated and energised to be more on the line of faith—active faith—not just faith in an historical way that we have believed and have had our sins forgiven; it required faith for that, but the mind of God is that, as christians, we are to be those who are living by faith. So it says, “The just shall live by faith”. May we be helped in this for His name’s sake.

PEGS AND CORDS Among the many parts of the tabernacle mentioned in Exodus 35 are “the pegs of the tabernacle, and the pegs of the court, and their cords”—small and humble items, but vital if the structure was to be kept firm and upright at all times and in all weathers. In a reading on this passage a brother remarked that if you could see much of a peg, it was not doing its job. A peg suggests out-of-sight faithfulness and stability—a brother or sister devoted to the Lord, and firm in the truth. The pegs were connected, some to the tabernacle and some to the pillars of the court, by cords—suggesting strong ties of love and faithfulness which sustain and strengthen what God has here in service and in testimony. Let us all be greatly concerned to be firmly fixed pegs, and supporting cords, and thus to “strengthen the things that remain”, Revelation 3: 2
